concepts.name: Periodization and Chronology of Prehistoric Phases
key_dimensions: Absolute and relative dating of Lower, Middle, Upper Palaeolithic; Mesolithic; Neolithic phases
Basis of classification: tool typology vs. subsistence strategy vs. geological period (Pleistocene/Holocene)
UPSC trap: overlapping date ranges and regional variation in periodization across India
Distinction between prehistory (no writing) and protohistory (contemporary written records by outsiders, e.g., Harappan)

concepts.name: Lower Palaeolithic Culture: Sohan and Acheulian Traditions
key_dimensions: Sohan (pebble/chopper-chopping tool) tradition vs. Acheulian (handaxe-cleaver) tradition — geographic distribution
Key sites: Sohan Valley (Pakistan), Attirampakkam (Tamil Nadu), Pallavaram, Hunsgi-Baichbal Valley
Tool types: handaxe, cleaver, chopper — raw materials (quartzite, chert) and knapping technique
UPSC trap: Attirampakkam's revised dating (~1.5 million years) challenging 'Out of Africa' timelines

concepts.name: Middle Palaeolithic Phase: Flake Tool Industries
key_dimensions: Transition from core tools to flake-based tools; Levallois and Mousterian technique parallels in India
Key sites: Nevasa (Maharashtra), Bhimbetka (Middle Palaeolithic layers), Narmada Valley
Narmada Man (Homo erectus/archaic Homo sapiens) — only Palaeolithic human fossil from India
UPSC trap: confusing Narmada fossil's classification and its stratigraphic context

concepts.name: Upper Palaeolithic Phase: Blade and Burin Industries
key_dimensions: Introduction of blade tools, burins, scrapers; use of bone and antler alongside stone
Associated with anatomically modern Homo sapiens; climatic shift at end of Pleistocene
Key sites: Bhimbetka upper layers, Patne (Maharashtra), Inamgaon (pre-Mesolithic layers)
Cave art beginnings at Bhimbetka — earliest phases attributed to Upper Palaeolithic

concepts.name: Mesolithic Phase: Microlithic Technology
key_dimensions: Defining characteristic: geometric microliths (lunates, triangles, trapezes, points) — size <5 cm
Subsistence shift: specialized hunting, fishing, gathering; semi-nomadic lifestyle
Key sites: Bagor (Rajasthan — largest Mesolithic site), Adamgarh (MP), Langhnaj (Gujarat), Sarai Nahar Rai (UP)
UPSC trap: Bagor shows cattle domestication evidence — blurring boundary between Mesolithic and early Neolithic

concepts.name: Bhimbetka Rock Shelters: Art and Habitation
key_dimensions: Continuous habitation from Lower Palaeolithic to early historical period — unique stratigraphic record
Rock paintings: chronological sequence — green/dark red (early) to multiple colours (later phases)
UNESCO World Heritage Site status (2003); discovered by V.S. Wakankar (1957)
UPSC trap: distinguishing rock art phases and associating specific motifs with specific periods (e.g., 'X-ray style' with later Mesolithic)

concepts.name: Mesolithic Burial Practices and Social Organization
key_dimensions: Evidence from Sarai Nahar Rai and Mahadaha (UP): extended burials, ochre use, grave goods
Indicators of incipient social differentiation and ritualistic behavior
Damdama site: largest Mesolithic burial ground — multiple burials suggesting community cemeteries
UPSC trap: comparing Mesolithic burials with Neolithic/Megalithic burials — overlapping features

concepts.name: Neolithic Revolution: Origins and Indian Context
key_dimensions: V. Gordon Childe's 'Neolithic Revolution' concept — food production, sedentism, polished stone tools
India's Neolithic is later and regional — NOT a uniform pan-India phenomenon
Three distinct Neolithic zones: Northwestern (Mehrgarh), Southern (Brahmagiri, Maski), Eastern/Northeastern (Chirand, Daojali Hading)
UPSC trap: assuming Neolithic = pottery everywhere — ash mound cultures of South India lack pottery initially

concepts.name: Mehrgarh: South Asian Neolithic Cradle
key_dimensions: Chronology: c. 7000 BCE — earliest Neolithic settlement in South Asia (Balochistan, Pakistan)
Evidence: wheat, barley cultivation; zebu cattle domestication; mud-brick structures
Continuity from Mehrgarh to Indus Valley Civilization — cultural bridge significance
UPSC trap: Mehrgarh is often tested as 'Pre-Harappan' or 'Early Harappan' — understanding its correct classification

concepts.name: Southern Neolithic: Ash Mound Culture
key_dimensions: Sites: Brahmagiri, Maski, Piklihal, Utnur, Kodekal, Budihal, Sanganakallu (Karnataka/AP)
Ash mounds (vibhutis): burnt cattle dung — interpreted as seasonal cattle-penning or ritual sites
Aceramic phase (absence of pottery in earliest levels) — distinguishing feature from other Neolithic zones
UPSC trap: confusing Southern Neolithic with Megalithic culture — both in Deccan but different periods

concepts.name: Eastern and Northeastern Neolithic
key_dimensions: Chirand (Bihar): cord-impressed pottery, bone tools; Senuwar — overlap with Chalcolithic
Daojali Hading (Assam) and Sarutaru: Southeast Asian cultural affinities — shouldered celts
Burzahom and Gufkral (Kashmir): pit dwellings, dog burials with humans, harappan connections
UPSC trap: Burzahom's Phase I (Aceramic) vs. Phase II (Ceramic) distinction and pit dwelling uniqueness in Indian context

concepts.name: Neolithic Tool Technology: Polished Stone and Ground Stone
key_dimensions: Shift from knapped/flaked tools to ground and polished tools — celts, axes, adzes, querns
Continued use of microliths alongside Neolithic tools — 'Microlithic Neolithic' contexts
Regional raw material variation: dolerite (South India), jade/nephrite (Northeast), basalt (Deccan)
UPSC trap: polished tools ≠ exclusively Neolithic — some Mesolithic sites show polishing; tool type alone insufficient for classification

concepts.name: Domestication of Plants and Animals in Indian Prehistory
key_dimensions: Crop evidence: wheat/barley (NW — Mehrgarh), rice (Koldihwa, UP — c. 6500 BCE debated), millets (South)
Animal domestication sequence: cattle/sheep/goat (Mehrgarh), dog (Burzahom burials), cattle (Bagor — Mesolithic context)
Koldihwa controversy: claims of earliest rice domestication debated due to dating issues
UPSC trap: conflating 'earliest evidence of rice in India' with 'earliest rice cultivation globally'

concepts.name: Pottery Traditions in Neolithic and Their Cultural Significance
key_dimensions: Hand-made vs. wheel-thrown pottery; cord-impressed, burnished, painted varieties across regions
Neolithic pottery types: grey ware (Burzahom), coarse red ware (South India Phase II), black burnished (Chirand)
Pottery as cultural marker: used to trace migration, trade, and cultural diffusion
UPSC trap: aceramic Neolithic phases (Mehrgarh I, Southern Neolithic Phase I) — pottery is NOT a universal Neolithic marker

concepts.name: Transition from Mesolithic to Neolithic: Continuity vs. Diffusion Debate
key_dimensions: Diffusionist model: Neolithic introduced via migration from West Asia through Mehrgarh corridor
Indigenous development model: evidence from Vindhyan sites showing gradual local transition
Cultural continuity evidence: persistent microlithic use in Neolithic contexts (Langhnaj, Adamgarh)
UPSC trap: the 'Neolithic Revolution' was not sudden in India — regional transitions over millennia

concepts.name: Neolithic Settlements and Village Life
key_dimensions: Settlement patterns: permanent villages, rectangular/circular huts, storage pits, granaries
Social organization: evidence for community labor, craft specialization, possible trade networks
Site examples: Mehrgarh (mud-brick town), Burzahom (pit dwellings), Piklihal (pastoral camps)
UPSC trap: not all Neolithic peoples were sedentary — pastoralist Neolithic (Piklihal) vs. agricultural Neolithic (Mehrgarh)

concepts.name: Overlap and Co-existence of Prehistoric Cultures: Chalcolithic Interface
key_dimensions: Neolithic-Chalcolithic overlap sites: Inamgaon, Navdatoli, Chirand — copper appears alongside stone tools
Three-Age System (Stone-Bronze-Iron) limitations in Indian context — stages often coexist regionally
Jorwe culture (Maharashtra) as a Chalcolithic phase growing out of local Neolithic traditions
UPSC trap: Chalcolithic cultures in India (Ahar, Kayatha, Malwa) are contemporary with late Harappan — not sequential

concepts.name: Key Prehistoric Archaeologists and Their Contributions
key_dimensions: Robert Bruce Foote: discovered Palaeolithic tools at Pallavaram (1863) — 'Father of Indian Prehistory'
V.S. Wakankar: discovery of Bhimbetka rock shelters; H.D. Sankalia: Nevasa, Inamgaon excavations
Jean-Marie Casal: Mehrgarh excavations; B.B. Lal: Hastinapur stratigraphy linking prehistory to history
UPSC trap: confusing discoverers with excavators; Robert Bruce Foote often tested as 'first to identify' vs. 'first to excavate'

concepts.name: Dating Methods Used in Indian Prehistory
key_dimensions: Relative dating: stratigraphy, typology of tools, faunal assemblages
Absolute dating: Radiocarbon (C-14) for organic material, Thermoluminescence (TL) for burnt flint/pottery, OSL for sediments
Potassium-Argon (K-Ar) and Electron Spin Resonance (ESR) for older Palaeolithic sites
UPSC trap: C-14 effective only up to ~50,000 years — Lower/Middle Palaeolithic sites require K-Ar or ESR

concepts.name: Protohistory: Definition, Scope and Harappan Civilization as a Case Study
key_dimensions: Protohistory defined: civilization has writing but it is undeciphered OR known only through others' records
Harappan script: undeciphered — makes IVC 'protohistoric' despite being a literate civilization
Contrast with Mesopotamia (contemporary written records exist about IVC — Meluhha references)
UPSC trap: IVC is classified as protohistoric (not prehistoric) — a frequently tested distinction; also Vedic period status debate
